newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: West Australia seeks interest in petrochem project.
newsitem.headline: West Australia seeks interest in petrochem project.

text.p: The Western Australia state government said on Friday it would call for companies worldwide to formally register their interest in developing a A$1 billion petrochemical plant in the state's northwest.
State Resources Minister Colin Barnett said he expected intense competition in the Pilbara Petrochemical Project from the major petrochemical producers.
"A whole range of companies have expressed interest," Barnett said. "That's why we need to start a formal process that is fair to all parties."
Barnett told a news conference that companies that have already expressed interest include the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, Dow Chemical Co, the Krupp group of Germany and the Samsung of South Korea.
"All the major international companies recognise this as a great opportunity and recognise that this gives easy access, low cost access into the Asian market," Barnett said.
Barnett said the registrations of interest period would open on July 19 and close on September 26.

Barnett said it would be an opportunity for proponents to register their interest in developing gas-processing chemical projects in the Pilbara mining province or southwest of the state which could be integrated with the petrochemical plant.
"The government has identified the development of a privately-funded petrochemical plant as the major resource development opportunity in W.A. this decade," Barnett said.
"I am confident the project will proceed and that it will be under construction by the turn of the century. It will be a major milestone for resource development in W.A.," he said.
As outlined at the news conference, the Pilbara Petrochemical Project would:
* be based on ethane and/or liquefied natural gas contained in natural gas coming on-shore from the North-West Shelf;
* cost between $A1 billion and $A1.5 billion, all of which would be privately funded;
* produce more than 500,000 tonnes a year of products worth $A1 billion for the plastics industry and more than one million tonnes a year of caustic soda for the mining industry

"(The Pilbara) is the ideal location in W.A. because of the region's close proximity to major Asian markets and the abundance of key raw materials such as solar salt and competitively-priced natural gas resulting from deregulation of the energy market in the state," Barnett said.

"The Asian region is expected to maintain very high growth in demand for petrochemicals during the next decade and planned petrochemical capacity in the region is not expected to meet this demand," Barnett said."Therefore, a petrochemical plant in the Pilbara could meet a significant proportion of this market."
